title: Tether reportedly sought a 20% fee from some crypto hack victims to reissue frozen USDT, Bloomberg reports
date_note: Both pages were published 25 November and give no earlier day for the Bloomberg report.
geo_basis: no location stated in the sources read
summary: Gizmodo and crypto.news, relaying a Bloomberg report, say Tether reportedly sought fees from some crypto hack victims seeking to recover frozen USDT. Gizmodo says a Tether lawyer told the acquirer of the Singapore exchange Bittok about a 20% reissuance fee. A Tether spokesperson said the fees it charges help fund that process as well as legal costs.
plain: Bloomberg, as relayed by Gizmodo and crypto.news, reports Tether sought a 20% fee from some hack victims to reissue frozen USDT. A Tether spokesperson said fees help fund the process and legal costs.
exec: Reported fees on returning frozen stolen USDT matter to firms that may need to recover funds after a crypto theft.
impact: Fee terms for returning frozen stolen USDT, per the Bloomberg report as relayed.

evidence.quote: about a 20% “reissuance fee” on any stolen USDT, Tether’s dollar-pegged crypto token

validation.note: Gizmodo and crypto.news both relay one Bloomberg report, which was not read; not independent.
